author: Max Torres
title: Oregon Safety Aaron Flowers 'Done for the Foreseeable future' According to Dan Lanning - NewsBreak
text:
By Max Torres ,
1 days ago
Oregon Ducks defensive back Aaron Flowers ahead of facing Montana State. (Photo by: Max Unkrich/ScoopDuckOn3) Oregon starting safety Aaron Flowers is expected to miss significant time with a shoulder injury according to head coach Dan Lanning .
“Aaron had surgery, so he’s gonna be done for the foreseeable future,” Lanning said following Wednesday’s practice. “Something that he tried to tough out, credit to him. Sometimes you can play through that, but you’re probably not gonna play as well. But it’s one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him.”
Flowers was ruled out for the UCLA game after sustaining his injury in Oregon’s 41-27 win over USC in Los Angeles last month. In four games this season the junior defensive back from Forney, Texas recorded 17 total tackles and one pass breakup.
Junior Peyton Woodyard and freshman Devin Jackson were called upon in his absence against the Bruins.
“Some good, some bad. It’s that,” Lanning said of what he saw from the two defensive backs. “But I think you look at where we’re at total in the game, I think there was some real positive.
“There was a touchdown run we gave up that we fit wrong at safety. That we should’ve had an extra hat there. But there was some positive. There’s still room for improvement from both, but I think there’s some bright spots there and certainly happy with the growth, what that’s looked like if we continue to grow. I think you can see all those guys back there.”
The Ducks could also call on freshman Jett Washington, who starts on every special teams unit for Oregon and grabbed two interceptions against Portland State earlier this year.
Oregon faces a 5-1 Nebraska team at 8:00 PM PT in Eugene this weekend.
